newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Dec hotel stays rise first time in four years.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Dec hotel stays rise first time in four years.

text.p: Early snowfalls and a weaker Swiss franc helped reverse a four-year slump in overnight stays in Swiss hotels during December, the Federal Statistics Office said on Friday.
Overnight stays in Swiss hotels in December rose 2.8 percent to 1.76 million with demand from Swiss citizens up 2.5 percent and that of foreign tourists by three percent, the office said.

The increase in December, however, was not enough to reverse the slump during the rest of 1996 and the office estimated that overnight stays fell by 4.9 percent in the whole year to 29.7 million. Compared with 1990, when there was a record number of visits to Swiss hotels, the decline in 1996 amounts to 16.9 percent.
The trend toward shorter stays in Swiss hotels also continued, the office added.
In addition to the fall in the value of the franc and heavy snowfalls, Christmas and New Year fell on favourable days that encouraged skiers to take longer holidays, the office said.
The strongest increase in December came from Belgian tourists, who increased their visits by 22 percent.
There was six percent rise in tourists from the Netherlands, a 4.5 percent rise in German tourists, a 3.9 percent rise in French tourists and a 3.6 percent rise in British tourists.
During 1996 overnight stays by Swiss citizens fell by around three percent while visits by foreigners fell by six percent.
The only bright spot was that tourists from South and East Asia as well as Australia continued to show up in higher numbers.
The strongest decline in overnight stays in 1996 was by British tourists, with a drop of 11 percent. Stays by German tourists fell 8.7 percent, and those by French tourists fell 8.1 percent.
